fact: Camtel operates four existing submarine cables for Cameroon (SAIL, WACS, SAT-3 and NCSCS, the Nigeria-Cameroon cable), with 2024 utilisation of 6%, 57%, 29% and 92% respectively per a Chamber of Accounts report of June 2024, as reported by Ecofin (article of 2025-12-10; landing stations not named).
L'Economie reports that the October 2025 internet disruption in Cameroon was attributed to a problem on the WACS submarine cable, described as the cable that links the country to the global network.
MINPOSTEL's Secretary General reported that in 2025 Camtel raised the capacity of the NCSCS submarine cable from 100 Gbps to 300 Gbps, with a study towards 2.4 Tbps.

Xalam Analytics states that Cameroon is connected to four submarine cables offering direct routes to Europe, South Africa and the Americas; the cables and landing stations are not named in the passages.

AFR-IX telecom states that the Ceiba-2 submarine cable (400 km, 40 Gbps, built Oct 2015 to Mar 2017) connects Malabo, Bata and Kribi in Cameroon, and Equatorial Guinea inaugurated its link to it on 4 June 2018; as_of is the inauguration date.

fact: Africa Business Insight (2026-05-25) states that Cameroon is connected to five submarine cable systems, without naming them or their landing stations.
Camtel staff say its network is meshed and redundant with 4 submarine cables, giving several exit routes; landing stations are not stated.
Anthony Same, CEO of ST Digital, refers to the presence of several submarine cables in Cameroon.
Camtel has three landing stations (Kribi, Limbe, Douala) giving access to the SAT3, WACS, NCSCS and SAIL submarine cables, per the ART report quoted by Ecomatin.
Camtel's capacity on these cables lets it provide international transmission services to national and sub-regional operators, per the ART report.
Sika Finance says Cameroon's submarine cable at Kribi is in use, and that Cameroon opened access to it to Chad in 2015.
OBS-CC says five submarine cables (SAT-3/WASC, WACS, NCSCS, SAIL, Ceiba-2) connect Cameroon to the world, landing at three towns: Limbe, Douala and Kribi.
Submarine Networks, relaying Business in Cameroon, says Cameroon is connected with five submarine cable systems (SAIL, WACS, SAT-3/WASC, NCSCS, Ceiba-2), all owned and operated by Camtel.
CAMTEL's 2026 product sheet says four submarine cable systems (SAT-3, WACS, SAIL, NCSCS) link Cameroon to Europe, Africa, Asia and the Americas through landing points at Douala, Limbe and Kribi.
CAMTEL's 2026 product sheet sells IPLC and IP transit to operators, ISPs and multinationals, with access to all landing points of SAT-3, WACS, SAIL and NCSCS.
Tchadinfos reports Camtel supplies capacity from its Kribi landing station, from which Chad's operators draw their international capacity.

Tchadinfos reports Camtel committed to supply Safitel capacity gradually, up to 200 G within six months, and to give Safitel and Sotel access to its monitoring platform for capacity supplied from Kribi.
The Chambre des comptes audit of Camtel says three submarine cables, WACS, NCSCS and SAIL (to Brazil), have been in service since 2015, with utilisation of 18.5%, 1.25% and 0.31% at end-2021.
